rows.why_long: Underdog higher 2.5 needs 56% per pick for your entry; fair view 66% (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line). Averaging 3.2 over the last 8 games, higher than 2.5 in 62% of them (raw 56%, shrunk 65%). Projects 3.5 (raw 65%, shrunk 66%).
why_points: The pick: Receptions higher 2.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line) is 66%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 3.5. This is the best number for the higher side.
Game log, most recent first: 8, 3, 3, 0, 0, 2, 4, 1. Weighted average 3.2; went higher than 2.5 in 4 of 8 games (62% recency-weighted).
Trending up: last 3 games average 4.7 vs 1.4 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±2.8, so the line is 0.3 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): +5% on his average.
PFF: DAL plays man on 31% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 30%); he gains 1.16 yds/route vs man and 1.63 vs zone → -0% from scheme.
PFF: DAL allows 1.54 yds/route to RBs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.29) → +24% against his usual opponents.
PFF: 52% of his targets are short (0-9 yds) (league 48%); DAL allows 7.7 yds/target there (league 6.6) → +2% from depth.
PFF: He lines up in the slot 60% of the time; DAL's slot defenders allow 1.63 yds per coverage snap (league 1.58, softer).
PFF: TEN's run blocking vs DAL's run defense: 1.2 yds before contact per carry expected (his usual 1.0, league 1.1); he adds 3.4 after contact → +3% per carry.
Projection: we expect 3.5 catches on average; in a typical game 3.1 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 0.6 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 56% and the matchup 65%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 65%, matchup 66%.
Bottom line: we give it 66% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: +10.0 points; that works out to about +18¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
Risks: low line - one play can decide it.

rows.rank_head: Faces the worst defense vs RB receiving (32nd of 32)
rows.why: Check the news first — news: lead role: Remains clear lead back; Spears on IR and Singleton inactive leaves Chestnut as backup. (FantasyData). No bet: we expect about 3.5 catches vs the 2.5 line — not enough to clear the price (needs 56% per pick on Underdog)
rows.why_long: Underdog lower 2.5 needs 56% per pick for your entry; fair view 34% (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line). Averaging 3.2 over the last 8 games, lower than 2.5 in 38% of them (raw 44%, shrunk 35%). Projects 3.5 (raw 35%, shrunk 34%).
why_points: The pick: Receptions lower 2.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line) is 34%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 3.5. Another app has a better number for the lower side; take that one.
Game log, most recent first: 8, 3, 3, 0, 0, 2, 4, 1. Weighted average 3.2; went lower than 2.5 in 4 of 8 games (38% recency-weighted).
Trending up: last 3 games average 4.7 vs 1.4 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±2.8, so the line is 0.3 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): +5% on his average.
PFF: DAL plays man on 31% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 30%); he gains 1.16 yds/route vs man and 1.63 vs zone → -0% from scheme.
PFF: DAL allows 1.54 yds/route to RBs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.29) → +24% against his usual opponents.
PFF: 52% of his targets are short (0-9 yds) (league 48%); DAL allows 7.7 yds/target there (league 6.6) → +2% from depth.
PFF: He lines up in the slot 60% of the time; DAL's slot defenders allow 1.63 yds per coverage snap (league 1.58, softer).
PFF: TEN's run blocking vs DAL's run defense: 1.2 yds before contact per carry expected (his usual 1.0, league 1.1); he adds 3.4 after contact → +3% per carry.
Projection: we expect 3.5 catches on average; in a typical game 3.1 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 0.6 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 44% and the matchup 35%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 35%, matchup 34%.
Bottom line: we give it 34% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: -22.0 points; that works out to about -39¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
Risks: low line - one play can decide it.
rows.glance_head: Pass: we expect about 3.1 in a typical game vs the 2.5 line — if anything the other side.
